points.title: Huntrix on stage
points.kid: The girls shine on stage AND fight demons in secret. Which job do you think is harder?
points.parent: Set up the movie's central image early: their singing isn't just showbiz — the fans' real connection to them literally powers the Honmoon, the barrier that protects everyone. Shine that protects people = the lantern. Hold that thought for when the Saja Boys arrive with the other kind of shine.

options.reply: Look at the glowing barrier when the fans sing along...

options.text: It powers the Honmoon — the barrier that keeps demons out
options.reply: YES. Their art is protection. When people connect through their songs, everyone gets safer. That's shine used as a lantern.
Not sleep — it keeps them OUT, by keeping people connected.

quiz.question: What does Huntrix's singing actually DO in this world?

points.title: The Saja Boys arrive
points.kid: The Saja Boys are SO catchy and everyone loves them instantly. Can you feel the difference between their shine and Huntrix's shine?
points.parent: Here's the idol trap made literal: the Saja Boys' shine is designed to make fans hand over their energy — to give up their paddle, not paddle harder. A lantern lights your way; an idol asks for your rowing. Fun family test for any star or influencer: after watching them, do you want to DO more, or just watch more?

options.text: A lantern makes you paddle more; an idol takes your paddle
options.reply: YES. Good heroes leave you stronger and more yourself. The Saja Boys' whole plan is to collect paddles.
Brightness isn't it — the Saja Boys are PLENTY bright. Look at what happens to the fans' energy.
The whole movie disagrees — watch what each kind of shine does to the people watching.

quiz.question: What's the difference between a lantern and an idol?

points.title: Gwi-Ma's voice
points.kid: Gwi-Ma doesn't fight with claws — he fights with a voice that tells people they're worthless. Have you ever heard a voice like that in your own head?
points.parent: The most psychologically precise villain in any of our three movies: shame as literal fuel. Gwi-Ma's whispers only work on what people already fear about themselves. The somatic skill from our curriculum applies directly — the shaming voice FEELS different in the body than the protecting one. Ask: where do you feel it when a mean thought shows up? Naming the body-place shrinks the voice.

options.reply: It's usually a whisper. Loudness isn't the weapon...

options.text: It repeats the fears people already carry
options.reply: YES. He can only use what shame already put there. Which means every secret told to a trusted person is ammunition taken AWAY from him.

options.text: It can control anyone at any time
options.reply: Watch who he CAN'T reach — people standing in their truth are terrible customers.
